```plato
//==
// # Remeshing
//
// The intermediates the remeshing algorithms of `remeshing.library.plato` pass
// between their passes. Nothing here is a new geometry representation: a mesh
// stays a `TriangleMesh3D` / `PolygonMesh3D` (`meshes.types.plato`) from one end
// of a remeshing pipeline to the other, and these types are the two things a pure
// language needs in order to REBUILD such a mesh instead of mutating one.
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Derived triangle connectivity
//  - Vertex rewrites
//  - Smoothing weights
//
// The design decision behind them, stated once here because both types exist to
// serve it: a remeshing operation is a WHOLE-MESH REBUILD driven by a decision
// taken against a single, unchanging input mesh. An in-place remesher splits an
// edge, invalidating every index it has, and then splits the next one; here every
// edge is judged against the same mesh, the decisions are collected into per-edge
// arrays, and one pass applies all of them at once. Operations that ADD vertices
// (split, subdivision) append their new points to the position array in a fixed
// block order and rewrite the face table by index arithmetic; operations that
// REMOVE vertices (weld, collapse, decimation) build a `VertexRemap` and apply it.
// Nothing is ever mutated, and no index is ever invalidated mid-pass.

//==
// # Derived triangle connectivity
//
// A triangle mesh stores positions and faces and nothing else, so every remeshing
// pass has to recover its edges first. `TriangleMeshTopology` is that recovery,
// reified: it is derived, read-only, and thrown away when the pass that built it
// produces its new mesh. It plays the role a half-edge structure plays in a
// mutable remesher, minus the part that makes a half-edge structure hard — it is
// never updated, only rebuilt.
//
// Corners are numbered as `CornerTable` (`topology.types.plato`) numbers them:
// corner c belongs to triangle c / 3 at slot c mod 3, and reads as the DIRECTED
// edge from its own vertex to the next corner's vertex. An undirected edge is a
// twin pair of corners, named by the lower of the two (a boundary corner names its
// own edge), and numbered by the rank of that naming corner — the same canonical
// -corner rule `meshes-polygon.library.plato` uses for `PolygonMesh3D`.

// The edges of a triangle mesh, recovered once and indexed both ways: from a
// corner to the undirected edge it runs along, and from an undirected edge back
// to the corner that names it. CornerEdges and CornerTwins have one entry per
// corner (three times the face count); UndirectedEdges and EdgeCorners have one
// entry per undirected edge. A corner with no twin is a boundary corner and
// stores -1.
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Typed indices (-1 means "none").
type TriangleMeshTopology
    implements IValue
{
    CornerEdges: Array<UndirectedEdgeIndex>;
    CornerTwins: Array<CornerIndex>;
    UndirectedEdges: Array<VertexPair>;
    EdgeCorners: Array<CornerIndex>;
}
```
